metadata.name: Virginia Electric and Power Company (Dominion Energy Virginia)
metadata.dollar_basis: Nominal dollars. Cumulative figures undiscounted unless labelled npv3_2026 (NPV at 3%, 2026 dollars). Bills are the average residential bill, $/month.
metadata.flows_note: Customer savings split residential / business by the residential share of sales (EIA-861, 2024).
metadata.share_sweep_note: Each scenario and pace re-run at utility_share 0.20 / 0.30 / 0.40 with every other input fixed (default 0.30). Value creation is held constant across shares: the share moves value between customers and the utility; it does not change what flexibility delivers.
metadata.objective_sweep_note: Each scenario and pace re-run with an additional savings objective of 0 / 2.5 / 5 / 10% of its base (default 0%, base dist_revenue_requirement, net of 20% cost to achieve), every other input fixed. The objective is additional to the other layers by assumption.
metadata.objective_sweep_run_note: Each objective_sweep level carries its full chart data under run (yearly, waterfall_usd_month, value_flows_m), built exactly as the top-level run block.
metadata.earnings_note: earnings_total_m = equity return on rate base + shared savings earnings; earnings_per_rate_base = earnings_total_m / rate base (wires + program regulatory asset).
metadata.advance_note: advance: each scenario with the customer dividend advance on (default off in the model): level bill credit for advance_credit_years from 2027 sized at 1.0 x the NPV (3%, 2026 $) of Cautious customer savings, financed at the after-tax WACC as a utility regulatory asset, recovered from the positive pool before sharing on a schedule that follows the sizing scenario pool; true-up pauses credits when behind schedule; recoveries capped so customers net saving is never negative. advance_stress: sized on Central, realized Cautious. worst_year_vs_bau = the largest shared-savings minus BAU average residential bill.
metadata.tornado_note: Tornado at Central (every input at central; low and high one at a time), per pace; change in the average residential monthly saving vs Central.
